titulo: Managing a Conversation: Turn-Taking, Interrupting, Repair
descripcion: At C2 you manage a conversation's overall shape, not just your own turns: noticing when someone hasn't spoken and drawing them in, redirecting a conversation that's drifted without announcing the redirection, and repairing someone else's stumble without drawing attention to it.

filas: So, coming back to the original question…
picking up their unfinished sentence naturally

ejemplos.texto: What's your read on this? You've been quiet.
So, coming back to the original question, where does that leave us?
—I think what you mean is that it needs more time.

notas: Drawing in someone who hasn't spoken is a management move, not just politeness — it changes what the conversation as a whole produces.
Redirecting without announcing it (so, coming back to…) is smoother than explicitly calling out the drift, which can feel like a correction.
Finishing someone else's stumbled sentence accurately and briefly helps them; doing it repeatedly or inaccurately undermines them.

contraste.es: Spanish has phrases for the same moves (¿tú qué opinas, Ana? – what's your take, Ana?; volviendo a lo de antes – going back to…), so the functions transfer. The work lies in building a ready repertoire of English phrases for each move.
contraste.de: German has phrases for the same moves (Was meinen Sie dazu? – What's your take?; um noch mal auf… zurückzukommen – going back to…). One difference: English meetings often use first names even in formal settings, where German would use Sie and a surname.
contraste.it: Italian has phrases for the same moves (tu che ne pensi? – what's your take?; tornando a… – going back to…), so the functions transfer directly.
contraste.fr: French has phrases for the same moves (et toi, qu'en penses-tu ? – what's your take?; pour revenir à… – going back to…), so the functions transfer directly.
contraste.pt: Portuguese has phrases for the same moves (e tu, o que achas? – what's your take?; voltando a… – going back to…), so the functions transfer directly.

errores: Redirecting so abruptly that it reads as a correction rather than a smooth return.
Finishing someone else's sentences so often that it takes over the conversation.
Drawing in a quiet person in a way that puts them on the spot rather than genuinely inviting them.

es: *A ver* as a turn-taking opener rendered as *To see…* instead of *Let's see…* or *Right…*.
de: *Moment mal* rendered as *Moment once* instead of *Hang on a second*.
it: *Allora* as a turn-taking opener rendered as *Then…* instead of *So…* or *Right…*.
fr: *Attends* rendered as a bare *Wait*, which sounds abrupt, instead of *Hang on a second*.
pt: *Espera aí* rendered as *Wait there* instead of *Hang on a second*.

traducciones.de: Entschuldigung, erzähl weiter — was wolltest du sagen?

redemittel.expresion: You two are closer than it sounds.

redemittel.expresion: Can we park that and come back to it?
redemittel.funcion: shelves a topic without dismissing it

traducciones.de: Können wir das kurz zurückstellen und später darauf zurückkommen?
traducciones.fr: Peut-on mettre cela de côté et y revenir ?

redemittel.funcion: manages the clock without rushing anyone

mision.consigna: Describe how you'd chair a public consultation on digital services where the discussion keeps drifting into complaints.
requisitos: one unannounced redirection, different from last time
drawing in someone from the back without putting them on the spot
a repair between two speakers talking past each other

microtareas.texto: Write three redirections that sound like continuations.
Write how you'd repair a misunderstanding about *digitalisation*.
Record 2 minutes chairing a talk on *red tape*. *We got a bit sidetracked, but…*

autochequeo: Has a quiet participant been drawn in naturally, not put on the spot?
Is any redirection smooth rather than an explicit correction?
Is a completed sentence for someone else accurate and brief?
Does the conversation as a whole feel managed, not just my own turns?
Have I avoided taking over by finishing sentences too often?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on managing the conversation as a whole: drawing others in, redirecting smoothly, repairing others' stumbles. Do not rewrite the text. Flag anything that feels abrupt or unnatural.
